source.title: Neural density functional theory in higher dimensions with convolutional layers.
source.authors: Felix Glitsch; Jens Weimar; M. Oettel

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the supplied text is the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: Reports results on generalization of convolutional density-functional networks to 2D hard-disk settings, measuring performance on held-out profiles and unseen potential geometries; this is a new physical-science setting outside the claim versions' named image and language tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out test-profile performance, but does not test memorization of arbitrary labels, standard gradient training on natural-label datasets, or the architecture/optimizer/batch-size/regularization/size comparisons and sharpness or memorized-example measurements in V1–V8. Its held-out profile results do not test those versions. Figures 3, 5, and 6 provide relevant explicit results on the broader generalization topic.
record.test_reason: The authors invoke large-batch drawbacks, citing Keskar et al., to motivate training on batches of 96 shuffled local windows instead of whole profiles. They report no controlled batch-size comparison. Their density-profile predictions, geometry extrapolation and kernel-count sweep do not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors demonstrate an FMT-inspired convolutional density functional for fully 2D hard-disk systems, accurate profile and unseen radial-geometry predictions, and substantially faster evaluation through convolutional implementation. They anticipate extension to other interactions and fully 3D systems, with smooth simulation training data requiring substantially greater effort.
record.recipe_differences: The work trains a convolutional density-functional model on simulation-generated density profiles and direct-correlation-function targets in a classical-fluid setting; it does not use the original claim's label-classification datasets or compare standard gradient recipes for label generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Potential type changes profile error: smooth sine potentials perform best, while plateaus and hard walls increase error. Increasing kmax improves the mean metric, but only slightly after a few kernels.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and held-out density profiles show no systematic performance difference; smooth sine potentials yield smaller errors than potentials with plateaus and hard walls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The learned density functional predicts held-out profiles accurately in the tested 2D hard-disk setting, with errors depending on potential geometry and discretization.

fits_no_version.finding: Pair-correlation predictions agree well with simulations across chemical potentials 0 through 5 for radial potentials excluded from training, with minor first-peak deviations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The learned density functional transfers to unseen radial test-particle geometries in the tested hard-disk setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing convolution-kernel count modestly reduces density-profile error averaged over all profiles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional kernels modestly improve this model's aggregate prediction accuracy; held-out improvement beyond interpolation is not established.

record.problems: The authors note finite-size effects from small simulation boxes, discretization errors around plateaus, and increased errors near hard-wall corners. The paper describes test-profile comparisons as plots without tabulated numeric values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label classification accuracy and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Held-out error beyond a width established to achieve zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section IV D compares computational implementations: the convolutional implementation of the earlier fully connected local-window network is equivalent in its action and faster to evaluate. This is not evidence for V3's generalization advantage.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization are not tested.
No width sweep around interpolation or test-error measurement by width.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparison.
No sharpness or other measure of the training-test gap.
No memorized-example removal and retraining experiment.
